events.title: Nuisance Bear
events.description:
“Truly groundbreaking” – Werner Herzog

“A David Attenborough doc shot by someone on shrooms.” – i-D Magazine

For thousands of years, polar bears have migrated along the shores of Hudson Bay in northern Canada. Today, that ancient rhythm collides with a human world of tourism, surveillance, and control. Nuisance Bear immerses viewers in the experience of a polar bear forced to navigate tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as climate change delays the freeze and pushes bears closer to human settlements. When a sacred predator is branded a “nuisance,” it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

Returning to Churchill, Manitoba—the self-styled “Polar Bear Capital of the World”—filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman expand their award-winning short into a feature guided by an Inuit narrator whose perspective resists simplification. Shot with striking intimacy and scale, the film observes bears that are constantly monitored, photographed, and redirected. In tracing this uneasy coexistence, Nuisance Bear becomes a meditation on how humans manage, commodify, and redefine wildlife—overturning the conventions of the nature documentary and reframing animals not as spectacle, but as active agents in a rapidly changing world.

events.title: American Psycho
events.description:
“Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh, my God. It even has a watermark.”

Before Christian Bale was the savior of Gotham, he was the chainsaw-wielding, business card-slinging scourge of Manhattan. Caught during the height of American Yuppieism in the late '80s, Patrick Bateman finds himself surrounded by friends who he hates and a culture he can’t stand. Can anyone blame him for allowing his nightly bloodlust to overflow into the day?

It’s hard to imagine anyone aside from Bale lecturing a soon-to-be victim on the cultural undertones found within Huey Lewis and The News’ “Hip to be Square,” all while wearing a raincoat and holding an incredibly shiny axe. But, what now seems meant to be almost wasn’t! The role was originally offered to none other than Leonardo DiCaprio. However, due to his newfound fame within the teenaged female demographic, Leo’s managers felt that a stint as a sociopathic mass murderer might somehow taint his image. I guess a career in murders and executions isn’t for everyone.

Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have to return some videotapes.

events.description: Jake Shimabukuro (born November 3, 1976, in Honolulu, Hawaii) is an American ukulele virtuoso and composer known for his fast and complex finger work. His music combines elements of jazz, blues, funk, rock, bluegrass, classical, folk, and flamenco. Shimabukuro has written numerous original compositions, including the entire soundtracks to two Japanese films, Hula Girls (2007) and the Japanese remake of Sideways (2009). Well known in Hawaii and Japan during his early solo career in the early 2000s, Shimabukuro became famous internationally in 2006, when a video of him playing a virtuosic rendition of "While My Guitar Gently Weeps" was posted on YouTube without his knowledge and became one of the first viral videos on that site. His concert engagements, collaborations with legendary musicians, media appearances, and music production have snowballed since then.

events.title: Flaming Creatures: The Films of Jack Smith
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 6:30pm / Screening 7pm

$15 / free or discounted for members

Curated & presented by Bradford Nordeen in association with Dirty Looks, The Lab and San Francisco Cinematheque

This program was initially organized in collaboration between Dirty Looks and LA Filmforum

This screening is dedicated to Agosto Machado (????–2026)—“a lady never tells.”

Jack Smith was an underground visionary in every sense of the word. Jack poured glitter into everything he made: pasty creatures, plastic fantasias and moldy monsters. He was a performance artist, filmmaker, playwright, photographer, socialist, aesthete, installation artist, scene-stealer, writer, interventionist. He built a theater and movie-studio in his rickety loft out of street debris; an intricate and child-like universe, Cinemaroc, was equal parts Baroque and broke. For a contingency of art and theater fags and dolls, Jack, as Charles Ludlam once eloquently put it, “is the daddy of us all.” And quixotically, the fact that he remains a somewhat underground or cult figure, as opposed to canonized creature, attests to his legacy.

Best known as a filmmaker, Jack made wild, indeterminable pictures. Flaming Creatures was his first finished film. Well, in truth, it’s his only finished film, since it ricocheted out of his hands when a trend of underground film raids made his opus a trophy for either side of a decency debate. Seized at the same time as Jean Genet’s Un chant d’amour (1950) and Kenneth Anger’s Scorpio...

When The Kettle Sings Tour

The Fretliners

Thursday, December 10 | The Freight

There is something happening between the mountains and the plains. A stirring in the dust. A song rising from the timber. Out of that landscape of grit and grace comes The Fretliners, a band carrying forward the oldest tradition in American music: telling the truth.

You can call them Colorado’s next great acoustic act. You can point to their Telluride and RockyGrass New Artist wins. You can talk about their musicianship, their harmonies, or their ability to command a room. All of those things are true. But they only tell part of the story.

The Fretliners are carving their own path through American music, drawing from bluegrass, Americana, folk, and rock to create something that feels both familiar and completely their own. Their songs carry the weight of long roads, changing seasons, lost loves, and the quiet hope that keeps people moving forward.

What separates The Fretliners is not just how they play, but what they have to say. Their writing feels rooted in something older than trends. They sing about places that shaped them, people who stayed, memories that linger, and the moments that remind us we are still connected to something real.

There is a kind of honesty in their music that cannot be manufactured. Each note feels lived-in,like old wood worn smooth by generations of hands. Each lyric feels like a conversation around a fire, a story passed down because it still matters.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Storefront Church
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Storefront Church

Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. Usually, that's even better.

Rooted in mirrored kinship and a captivating vocal blend, Lucius — the Grammy-nominated indie-pop duo of Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig — are songwriters of rare emotional precision, building one of contemporary music’s most enchanting, harmonic sounds. Their voices, described by the Los Angeles Times as “otherworldly,” move in perfect tandem: two instruments so attuned they read as one. Rolling Stone called their most recent album, 2025’s self-titled “the best album of their career” — a distinction earned through hard-won vulnerability, as Wolfe and Laessig turn inward to explore motherhood, relationships, and the quiet complexities of a life shared. The New Yorker wrote that the record “reaches the pinnacle of a vibrant, harmonic enterprise.”

The arc of their catalog is one of continuous, confident evolution. Their debut, Wildewoman, announced a singular voice — dual lead vocals wrapped in retro charm, which The New York Times praised the live show that year as “the best musical performance of any kind.”

Good Grief introduced a sleeker, synth-driven palette, while Second Nature — produced by Brandi Carlile and Dave Cobb — was celebrated by the Los Angeles Times with its “lush synths and sleek disco grooves under the women’s laser-guided vocals.”

events.title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Holiday show
events.description:
Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –
“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”
But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”
Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.
From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.
What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

events.title: Understanding Attachment Trauma & Building Resilience with Mindfulness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller
We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.
This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.
If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.
Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

events.title: Eyes Wide Shut
events.description:
In IT’S A WONDERFUL LIFE, Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey, at the height of his suicidal despair and panic, imagines a world in which he doesn’t exist. Stanley Kubrick goes one step further in sending Tom Cruise down an odyssey of sexual confusion and paranoia to learn the true meaning of Christmas.

Adapted from the Austrian short story Traumnovelle, Kubrick’s final film peeks us into the privileged world of Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (Cruise and Nicole Kidman), two well-to-do attractive socialites who, by all accounts, have it made. In a marijuana-fueled argument, Alice reveals thoughts of infidelity that send Bill into an existential panic, leading to an absurdist walkabout through New York that involves – you guessed it – a mysterious sex cult run by a shrouded aristocracy.

Did Kubrick make this to break up Cruise and Kidman’s marriage? How much did he know about mysterious sex trafficking rings? Did Sydney Pollack originate the shirtless-in-suspenders look? Clearly, the film poses more questions than it answers. For certain, EYES WIDE SHUT is a brutally funny sexscapade that puts an ellipses at the end of Kubrick’s storied career – and, most importantly – stands as a crucial text for our modern world. Fidelio!

events.description: This December, the PWC joins forces with the Palo Alto Chamber Orchestra to perform Vivaldi’s beloved Gloria. In addition to Vivaldi’s masterwork, the second half of our winter program celebrates the season with sacred and contemporary holiday treasures. Experience the luminous anticipation of Elaine Hagenberg’s O Come Emmanuel, Joan Szymko’s spirited Hodie, and Ann Callaway’s radiant Alleluia, Vidimus Stellam, paired with the otherworldly textures of Cindy Cox’s Wakah-Chan. We uplift traditions of community, reflection, and peace through Bernice Johnson Reagon’s stirring Seven Principles and Karen Siegel’s contemplative Oseh Shalom. The festivities draw to a heartwarming close with the gentle tenderness of Eleanor Daley’s Lullaby Carol and the timeless splendor of John Rutter’s setting of Silent Night. Join us 30 minutes before each performance for a pre-concert talk, and stay for a post-concert reception.

events.title: “Castro on Fire”: A Queer Resistance Walking Tour by Unspeakable Vice
events.description:
LOCATION

GLBT Historical Society Museum

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

$35; Museum admission included in tour

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

June McDoom

There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own.

She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition.

She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for.

Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive....

events.title: Little Women (2019)
events.description:
Having already once revolutionized the coming-of-age story with her debut LADY BIRD, Greta Gerwig has somehow outdone herself with this gorgeous and thoroughly original rendition of the beloved Louisa May Alcott classic. Bringing her effusive humor, authenticity, and irresistible warmth to the otherwise mannered Civil War-era New England, Gerwig's adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN breathes visceral new life into the March sisters – portraying them as unique, complicated, flawed, and astonishingly human. So human that you will leave the theater wanting to text Jo March and, for several reasons, this will not be a possibility.

You may also find it physically impossible not to chef's kiss at the cast, which is as close to pitch-perfect as it gets. Starring Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, and Eliza Scanlen as Beth, LITTLE WOMEN also features Laura Dern (!), Meryl Streep (!), Bob Odenkirk (!), and Timothée Chalamet as the dashing but lovelorn Laurie (!!!).

Save for a fireworks show, sky-written ode, or Mount Rushmore-type situation, we cannot recommend this rich, heartrending wonder of a film anymore. Its timeless charm is sure to capture the hearts of little women (and men) everywhere.

events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Yaelokre

Sunday, December 13 | The Castro

If you ever feel as if music has lost its capacity for surprise, the beguiling wonder and infinite creativity of Yaelokre will respark your belief. The Filipino-Icelandic artist – real name Keath Ósk (they/it) – fuses three imaginative strands to their visionary expression: intimate, innocent folk infused with leftfield surrealism and instant pop accessibility; artwork which is intricately detailed and beautifully alluring; and storytelling which brings personal experience and poetry into rich, fable-like narratives. What’s more, all three of these elements are crafted by this one visionary artist.

The scale of the fantastical world they have created is vast, both in terms of narrative and lore. But its essence is relatively simple. The songs are set in the fictional world of Meadowlark and chart the adventures of four masked children who comprise a musical ensemble known at The Lark: Cole Seymour, Clémente Dearworth, Peregrine August, and Kingsley. They perform as representatives of The Harkers, mythical beings who express the fundamental principles of nature, wonder and chaos. What’s more, Yaelokre voices all of the different characters within their universe.

events.title: Bitter Christmas
events.description:
Check out IN THE MOOD FOR ALMODÓVAR, our limited series celebrating three earlier works by Pedro Almodóvar.

The incomparable Almodóvar has been rendering the life of the creative mind on screen for five decades, with exquisite attention to every nuance of both aesthetic design and human emotion. With his complexly conceived latest, he uses a metacinematic framework to explore the artist’s tenuous relationship between fiction and reality. The sublimely expressive Bárbara Lennie stars as Elsa, a well-known actress suffering from debilitating migraines whose directorial efforts had failed upon release but have become cult classics. While trying to maintain a relationship with her loyal boyfriend Bonifacio (Patrick Criado), a fireman moonlighting as a stripper, she becomes inspired by the travails of her friends to write a new script.

Yet Elsa’s story is itself a story—being written by Raúl (Leonardo Sbaraglia), an Almodóvar-esque filmmaker who is, in turn, taking his cues from the lives of those around him. Mixing the irreverence of early Almodóvar with the somber melodrama of his later work, Bitter Christmas insightfully details the vampiric nature of artistic creation and how we use fiction to try and right the wrongs of our lives.

“With its moving musical interludes, comic patter and outrageously chic production design, Bitter Christmas is another dazzling, late-period jewel” — Little White Lies

Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Pokey LaFarge
with Cicada Rhythm
Wednesday, December 16 | Bimbo's 365 Club

For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. Rent Money now sees him pushing forward yet again in what can be safely declared his finest collection to date, both as an heartfelt expression of personal experience and as no-nonsense social commentary. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own.

“People are always going to tell you what they think you should play,” says Pokey LaFarge, “what you should sing about, how you should sound, how you should look, how you should act. And I’ve always just been like, nah. Nope. I’ve just completely gone my own way, and...

events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Robber Robber

Pinpointing the specific catalyst for an avalanche can be slippery — any combination of classic elements, human interference, or freak accident can trigger disaster — and documenting these precise moments often rests on serendipitous reflexes. On Two Wheels Move the Soul, Robber Robber offer themselves as ignition and capture every sound in the wake. Involuntarily thrust into the throws of rootless nomadism, Robber Robber ringleader Nina Cates collects a series of pressurized vignettes to assemble the Burlington quartet’s thrillingly explosive sophomore album.

Two Wheels Move the Soul was written and recorded throughout the winter of 2024 and 2025, a season of Cates’ life characterized by near-constant upheaval. In January of 2025, Cates (and Robber Robber co-founder) Zack James were displaced from their longtime home at the behest of a landlord’s call to have their building demolished. In a moment’s notice — and amidst a particularly brutal Vermont winter — Cates and James were left to fend for themselves. Luckily, the two were able to tap a deep well of support within their community, finding respite on the couches of Lily Seabird, Greg Freeman, and Thus Love’s Echo Mars. An unused attic provided their longest arrangement.

After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.

Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, and Macie Stewart are a trio who utilize string instruments, voices, and manual tape effect processing to craft compositions from alternately tranquil and disquieting improvised music. The three musicians are individually rooted in deep sound exploration, multi-disciplinary composition, and all manner of cross-genre collaboration. The musical ground covered by their solo practices is correspondingly expansive, and their individual recording and performance credits read as a veritable who’s who, ranging from DIY darlings to household names of experimental avant-garde, electronic, indie rock, and more.

Their influences are vast — dispatched with more playful ease than a trio of string instruments is typically approached with, and just as likely to be found in the cloud-obscured mountains of Donegal, the low-rent cacophony of a Midwestern basement, or the revelatory expanse of the Nurse With Wound list as in the storied halls of the academy. Touchstones and areas of interest aside, the main thing that Johnson, Kohl, and Stewart engage with in BODY SOUND is: listening and reacting.

events.title: Venna
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Venna

Friday, December 8 | The Castro

After two EPs and an illuminating start to his career, Grammy Award-winning saxophonist Venna releases his debut album, MALIK.

For Venna, it’s been a whirlwind of a journey to arrive at this point. He’s spent the better part of three years on the road touring, while coming back to London intermittently. In the spaces he finds himself in as a musician, he’s often the youngest in the room. This period gave him the confidence to embark on this next stage of his career.

“Every experience, every memory, every conversation, anything new, any encounter has influenced how this album sounds. I might like a particular guitar tone from it, and then I bring it into my world. Everything has come and conjured into one place, and it’s beautiful to also hear and see,” Venna says.

Speaking on how he found the words to sing: “Does anyone really have the words to say? I don’t know. I don’t know if I had the words to say. I just conjured words and thoughts and tried to make art out of it.”

events.title: Florencia Ramirez, The Kitchen Activist
events.description:
Saturday, December 19, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Florencia Ramirez is the author of The Kitchen Activist: Your Step-by-Step Guide to Creating a Planet Smart Kitchen and Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRWs Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times. She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage

events.title: Elvin Bishop
events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description:
Ever since Rock & Roll and Blues Hall Of Famer Elvin Bishop first hit the scene with the Paul Butterfield Blues Band back in 1965, he's blazed his own musical trail. Whether he was playing raw, eye-popping blues, or penning the evergreen radio hit Fooled Around And Fell In Love, or touring the world for decades delivering his original, good-time countrified blues, Bishop has always inspired his fans with his rowdy guitar playing and witty, slice-of-life songs. Rolling Stone calls Bishop "a legendary guitarist" whose playing is "impeccable and spirited...a distinguished American player."

Late in 2015, Elvin Bishop formed The Big Fun Trio, with Bishop on guitar and vocals, and his friends Bob Welsh on piano and guitar and Willy Jordan on cajón (a hand-played Peruvian drumbox) and vocals. After playing just a handful of live dates, the group's instantly crowd-pleasing music and undeniable chemistry took the blues world by storm. With the release of their self-titled CD in 2017, media and fan response was immediate and overwhelming. OffBeat said The Big Fun Trio was "intricate, funky and uplifting," declaring them, "consistently great." Presented by OUTlook and Frameline

Dubbed “SF’s hottest new holiday tradition” by the San Francisco Chronicle, Frameline’s fourth annual Carol Day returns to its home at the Roxie Theater. Shake up your martinis, don your gloves (and gay apparel) for a costume contest, and get ready to be flung out of space — again.

Set during Christmastime in 1950s New York, Todd Haynes’ adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s The Price of Salt centers on shy, aspiring photographer Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), whose world changes when she meets the elegant Carol Aird (Cate Blanchett). As Carol struggles to maintain custody of her daughter amid a heated divorce, she and Therese develop a secret-yet-passionate romance that changes them both irrevocably.

Featuring a stunning screenplay from Phyllis Nagy; memorable supporting turns from Sarah Paulson, Kyle Chandler, and Jake Lacy; and wholly transportive production design and costuming, Carol remains one of queer cinema’s most exquisite films.

events.title: Red Rocket
events.description:
Burnt out by the LA adult film scene, washed-up porn star Mikey Saber (Simon Rex) heads back to his old stomping grounds in small-town Texas. After a not-so-successful attempt at reconnecting with his estranged wife, Lexi (Bree Elrod), he forms an instant connection with Strawberry (Suzanna Son). Soon he’s juggling jealous exes, new love, and drug-dealing locals, all with a smile on his face. Who says you can’t go home again?

The audacious new film from writer-director Sean Baker (THE FLORIDA PROJECT, TANGERINE), starring Simon Rex in a magnetic, live-wire performance, RED ROCKET is a darkly funny and humane portrait of a uniquely American hustler and the hometown that barely tolerates him.

Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

events.title: P L A Y E R S L A Y O V E R
QUEERSADA 2026: A Queer Posada
events.description:
A catered meal, chosen family vibes, and a place to kick it, all on Christmas Day.

For the fourth year, our annual FREE community meal returns!
It's a party, with catered food, movies on the screens, and chosen family vibes all afternoon.

We'll have pozole, pan con pavo, and more on the menu. The bar will be open (cash and credit card accepted) for any drinks you need. The food is on us, the drinks are on you.

How can you contribute? Bring a dessert you think people would like. Anything is a good thing!

And here's the thing: whether you celebrate the holiday or not isn't what we are concerned with.

The reality is, this can be a very challenging day for our community. Isolation, disconnection, hunger...

There is no reason we can't come together to make sure everybody has a safe, affirming place to go, and a good, dignified meal to eat, all in a familiar space.

And that's the thing: community is for everyone, regardless of age, income, professional or academic background, body type, and so on.

Questions? Follow us on IG and send us a DM: @boss.ideahouse

The event is free, but we are asking for each person coming to RSVP so we can keep an eye on the food and seating availability.

events.title: Vienna Teng
events.description:
Vienna Teng

Sunday, December 27 | The Freight

Some songs are the life of the party. Vienna Teng's are the back-porch conversation you still remember years later.

Her subversive choral piece "The Hymn of Acxiom” turns up in media literacy classes as well as drum corps shows (plus David Byrne’s blog, and the occasional flash mob choir in government buildings). The angst and effervescence in “Stray Italian Greyhound” has inspired anime music videos - and bridge-building political conversations.

Americana-tinged "City Hall" has quietly become a queer anthem, a soundtrack for coming-out journeys. The electro-pop exhortations of “Level Up” have powered many a doctoral dissertation, first novel, and courageous battle with illness. “Harbor” is a beloved first dance at weddings and a graduation gift. “Lullabye For A Stormy Night” has been woven into countless bedtime rituals. These are songs that not only age well, but remain trusted friends throughout people’s lives.

It helps that Vienna's sound has never stood still. Her warm, delicate mezzo has drawn listeners since 2002, when her debut Waking Hour landed appearances on NPR's Weekend Edition, The Late Show with David Letterman, and the top of Amazon’s charts. But she’s built different worlds around that voice from album to album: the string-laced intimacy of Warm Strangers, the hushed jazz of Dreaming Through the Noise, the eclectically ambitious Inland Territory, the shimmering electronica of Aims.

She’s world-built for othe...

events.title: The Apartment
events.description:
A young upstart, C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon), will do anything to move up in the world...even loan out his apartment to the higher-ups for their romantic flings and extramarital trysts. All seems relatively fine and dandy until C.C. finds a romance of his own.

Billy Wilder is a genius – there aren't enough words in the world to describe all the films he's made and express how much he means to cinema – but in 1960, Wilder wrote and directed a perfect movie. I'm not saying this to sell you on the idea of seeing this film at the Alamo; I'm stating it as a fact. There are very few instances where you watch a movie and realize you are witnessing pure magnificence in that moment. Sometimes you think about a movie after the fact, and it gets better and better until you begin to love a movie you previously only really liked. THE APARTMENT is NOT one of those movies. It is a movie where, within 15 minutes of watching, you realize it is unlike anything you have ever seen before. Jack Lemmon is amazing, Shirley MacLaine is a full-on pixie dream girl, and the chemistry and dialogue snap and sparkle like you wouldn't believe.

events.description:
An alcoholic, out-of-work teacher takes a job as the wintertime caretaker of a snowy resort. He brings his wife and young son with him. He wants to get some writing done. Things take a very dark turn...

THE SHINING is Stanley Kubrick’s chilling symphony of deft manipulation: Wendy Carlos’ score alternating with Ligeti compositions, Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall’s push-and-pull performances, and the omniscient Steadicam taking the whole thing in. THE SHINING transcends any trappings of paperback adaptation or genre exercise to become one of the most elementally terrifying works of art of the 20th century. Come lose yourself in its marvelous madness on the big screen, where it forever belongs.

We all know those couples. They see each other from across the room, they meet, and wham! They’re desperately in love.

That’s not the case for Harry and Sally. In fact, when they meet, they don’t particularly like each other. Sally is earnest and good. Harry is cynical and depressive. It’s not a match made in heaven.

But lovers of rom-coms know that opposites have a way of attracting.

events.title: El Grupo de Apoyo Latino
events.description:
El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

events.title: Mars Attacks!
events.description:
How do you follow the success of gargantuan blockbusters like BATMAN and BATMAN RETURNS? Well, if you’re oddball director Tim Burton, you decide to make a campy, violent, big-budget alien invasion comedy based on a series of sci-fi trading cards from the 1960s.

With an absurdly star-studded cast, including Pierce Brosnan, Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Danny DeVito, Michael J. Fox, Martin Short, Natalie Portman, Jack Black, Sarah Jessica Parker's head on a chihuahua’s body, and Jack Nicholson in two different roles, MARS ATTACKS! is a demented piece of retro-pop madness that represents Tim Burton at his very best. If you've never seen this epic, raucously funny cult classic, don't miss your chance to experience it on the big screen.

events.title: Megalopolis
events.description:
Like the famed empire that Francis Ford Coppola’s epic passion project is styled after, MEGALOPOLIS is a towering, monumental spectacle that most people will think about at least once a day. The City of New Rome is at a crossroads. At one end sits Cesar Catilina (Adam Driver), the idealistic artist striving for a utopian future, and at the other sits Mayor Franklin Cicero (Giancarlo Esposito), a powerful figure perpetuating greed, special interests, and partisan warfare. Their titanic struggle will shake the foundations of their city and lay the groundwork for a new tomorrow.

As engrossing and ambitious as you would expect from the filmmaker behind THE GODFATHER and APOCALYPSE NOW, MEGALOPOLIS is an unforgettable vision that could only have come from Coppola. Of course, he didn’t do it alone, and everyone in the unbelievable cast (including Driver, Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Laurence Fishburne, and more) delivers some of the most memorable performances of their careers.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description:
Lord Huron was created by Los Angeles-based artist Ben Schneider in 2010. After writing and recording two independent EPs (Into the Sun and Mighty) on his own, demand grew for Lord Huron to perform live. Schneider recruited friends Mark Barry (percussion), Miguel Briseño (bass) and Tom Renaud (guitar). Having first played music together at the tender age of 12, the group reunited and quickly hit their stride, transforming the project into a full-fledged live band.

Lord Huron’s debut LP Lonesome Dreams was released in 2012 followed by Strange Trails in 2015. The latter featured the multi-platinum single “The Night We Met,” which has gone on to become one of Spotify’s Top 40 most-streamed songs of all time. In 2018, Lord Huron earned widespread critical acclaim and a Top 5 debut on the Billboard Top 200 with their third album, Vide Noir– while their following LP Long Lost garnered praise from NPR, Time, Los Angeles Times, Spin and Stereogum and sparked performances on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, The Late Late Show with James Corden and CBS This Morning: Saturday. Their latest album The Cosmic Selector Vol. 1 was released in 2025 and brought the band’s live show into their largest venues to date, including Madison Square Garden in NYC and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

Live On The Stoop began as a series of pop-up shows in the Fillmore District with The Top Chefs, a collective of musicians rooted in the city. It has since evolved into a platform where artists from around the world can reimagine their songs live with the band. Now, we're bringing the Stoop experience to The Independent, just two blocks away from the home where the movement began.

This show won't simply recreate the pop-ups that our neighbors have come to know and love. It's a narrative-driven multimedia stage production celebrating San Francisco's musical history, from the Fillmore jazz era to the Summer Of Love to mobb music and beyond. If you love this city and its true culture, you won't want to miss it.

events.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (in 70mm)
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
2001: A Space Odyssey (in 70mm)

Friday, January 8 | The Castro

Kick off the new year with the ultimate cinematic journey. On Friday, January 8, 2027, Stanley Kubrick’s masterwork 2001: A Space Odyssey returns to the historic The Castro Theatre for an exclusive, large-format screening presented in glorious 70mm.

An imposing black structure provides a connection between the past and the future in this enigmatic adaptation of a short story by revered sci-fi author Arthur C. Clarke. When Dr. Dave Bowman (Keir Dullea) and other astronauts are sent on a mysterious mission, their ship’s computer system, HAL, begins to display increasingly strange behavior, leading up to a tense showdown between man and machine that results in a mind-bending trek through space and time.

With its themes of humanity vs. machinery, 2001: A Space Odyssey serves as a timelier-than-ever cautionary tale about the human race’s never-ending thirst for technological advancement. Don’t miss your chance to see this sci-fi classic on the Castro screen!

events.description:
SF’s Conservatory of Flowers Free First Tuesdays (Golden Gate Park)
Conservatory of Flowers
Whether you’re a native San Franciscan, a visitor from the other side of the world, or a budding botanist, the Conservatory of Flowers, located in Golden Gate Park, offers an intimate, up-close experience with nearly 2,000 species of rare, exotic, and endangered plants from more than 50 different countries.
Opened in 1879, the wood and glass greenhouse is the oldest existing conservatory of its kind in the Western Hemisphere.
Conservatory of Flowers’ Free Admission Day
First Tuesday of Every Month
100 JFK Dr., Golden Gate Park, San Francisco
FREE for everyone
Admission is normally free for SF residents ($12 for non-SF residents), but it’s free for all visitors on the first Tuesday of every month.
The Conservatory will also continue offering free or reduced admission through Museums for All, a program to bring free or reduced admission to San Francisco residents who receive public beneﬁts, including Medi-Cal and CalFresh. Plus, there’s free admission for Military & Veterans and children 4 and under.

Hours:
Thursday-Tuesday
10am – 4:30pm
Last entry at 4pm
Free Day: First Tuesday of the Month
Enjoy our winter light show, Photosynthesis, beginning 30 minutes after sunset every night. The show is free to the public and is about 30 minutes long.

events.title: Free Behind-the-Scenes Talk: How SF Neo-Futurists Run 100 Shows a Year (SF Main Library)
events.venue: SFPL Main Library Steve Silver Room (4th Floor)
events.description:
SF Neo-FuturistsLearn what it takes to write, direct and perform 100 SHOWS A YEAR as a small group of artists who also RUN THE BUSINESS together. It’s not a sitcom, it’s The San Francisco Neo-Futurists. They put on the Infinite Wrench, the show the SF Chronicle calls one of “22 San Francisco things everyone must do!”
They’ll pull back the curtain on how they operate as a non-hierarchical consensus-based collective to organize performance space, run committees, budget and raise funds and ultimately put on a show every week. They’ll also cover their process for writing new material for a new cast of performers to put on a different show every Friday and Saturday night.
The SF Neos are a collective of wildly prolific artists dedicated to the perpetual creation of experimental theatre that is immediate, ephemeral, accessible and cheap. They believe the stage is an extension of daily life: they perform as themselves in a non-illusory, interactive style that challenges the audience to create alongside them as active participants with a voice of their own. They respect and uplift each other on and off stage through non-hierarchical accountability, collective decision-making and anti-oppression practice of all kinds.

events.title: Free Millennial Punk Documentary Screening + Q&A
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer© SWR/ Felix Bundschuh
What does punk mean when it’s already been declared dead? Millennial Punk – Eine Subkultur in Zeiten der Digitalisierung looks at the punk scene of the 1990s and early 2000s through the voices of the people who lived it.
We’re screening the first two episodes of the four-part documentary series. After the screening, writer Diana Ringelsiep and director Felix Bundschuh join us for a conversation and Q&A.

The series was made in 2024. Musicians, journalists and activists from the scene look back on a time when punk was often written off as a thing of the past. Beyond the music, the series explores punk’s lasting ties to anti-discrimination, anti-fascism and diversity, and asks what it takes to keep Punk’s not dead! alive in an increasingly digital world.
Episodes 3 and 4 screen the following evening, November 5.

events.title: Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerStock ImageIn this three week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques while learning the basics of drawing portraits from photographs.
Drawing human faces requires the same basic drawing skills that one employs for any subject – observing proportion, flattening shapes, and utilizing line or value to convey volume. But the conceptual weight of human faces tends to intimidate artists. When drawing any subject, the hardest skill is simply learning to see, a skill that anyone can be taught, practice, and hone. This course will focus on the practice of looking, and discovering strategies to find objectivity when rendering portraits.

This class is for anyone who wants to practice and advance their drawing skills – beginners, those who haven’t practiced in years, or any artists who just want to learn new techniques and practice their skills with consistent feedback and guidance. Through demonstration, practice, and reflective discussion, this class will explore the foundations of rendering human expression with classical drawing techniques in a low pressure environment.
Observational drawing gives all artists a foundation of practical knowledge and skills that infinitely expands the possibilities of what one can create. If your ideas feel limited by your drawing skills, if you feel frustrated or stuck in your painting practice, or if you simply want to start drawing and are looking for a place...

events.title: Free SF Fútbol Night: Roll Fog Film Preview + Panel (KALW)
events.description:
KALW

Join KALW for an evening exploring the culture, community & future of fútbol in San Francisco, with filmmakers, photographers, and fans.

Soccer is about more than what happens on the pitch. It’s about community, identity, creativity, and the people who keep the game beautiful.
Join KALW for an evening exploring the culture and future of fútbol in San Francisco, featuring filmmakers, photographers, designers, and community builders working at the intersection of soccer and local culture.

At the center of the conversation is Roll Fog, a documentary by filmmaker Daniel Díaz about the oldest community-owned soccer club in the United States, whose loyal supporters face the loss of their home amid the arrival of a new, billionaire-backed team. What happens when a community’s connection to the game is threatened, and what does it take to keep that spirit alive?
Through a preview of Roll Fog, a short film from Fútbol by the Bay, and a conversation among voices from the local scene, we’ll explore who gets to shape the future of San Francisco soccer, what makes its culture unique, and why the stories around the game matter as much as the action on the field.

Daniel Diaz
Colombian-British filmmaker and cultural producer, based in San Francisco since 2019. Work focuses on belonging, memory and fútbol. “Director of upcoming documentary feature film, Roll Fog.

events.title: Pluralities Project: “The Negro Artist” Screening & Live Awards
events.venue: McKenna Theatre, San Francisco State University
events.description:
Nik HeftmanPluralities Project: “The Negro Artist” Screening & Live Awards
Join the Documentary Film Institute at San Francisco State University on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 5:30 PM at McKenna Theatre for the closing-night event of the sixth Pluralities Project. The evening features a screening of The Negro Artist, presented by filmmaker Nik Heftman and poet Caleb Rainey, followed by the Accomplice Awards honoring artists, activists, and cultural figures who have brought important issues to light. This year’s posthumous honorees include pioneering Black journalist Belva Davis and her longtime producer George Osterkamp, along with influential cultural critic, musician, and artist Greg Tate. Part of the sixth Pluralities Seminar, this event brings together film, poetry, journalism, and cultural history to celebrate the people who challenge narratives and shape our understanding of the world.

events.title: Filmscreening: Millennial Punk: Episodes 3 & 4
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer© SWRWe’re screening the final two episodes of Millennial Punk – Eine Subkultur in Zeiten der Digitalisierung, Diana Ringelsiep and Felix Bundschuh’s four-part documentary series on the punk scene of the 1990s and early 2000s.
The series was made in 2024. Musicians, journalists and activists from the scene look back on a time when punk was often written off as a thing of the past. Beyond the music, the series explores punk’s lasting ties to anti-discrimination, anti-fascism and diversity, and asks what it takes to keep Punk’s not dead! alive in an increasingly digital world.

Episodes 1 and 2, followed by a conversation with the filmmakers, screen on November 4.

events.title: Free Art + Science Talk: Inside the Kelp Forest
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizersfpl
Artist, author and designer Josie Iselin shares the creative journey behind her work exploring seaweed and kelp forests. Drawing from art, science, history and close observation of the natural world, she will discuss how her fascination with marine algae developed into books and projects that reveal the beauty, complexity and ecological importance of these underwater ecosystems.
Josie Iselin is a photographer, author and designer whose recent work explores seaweed, kelp and coastal ecosystems. Her newest book, The Mysterious World of the Bull Kelp Forest (Heyday Books, 2026), features illustrations by Ellen Litwiller and builds on her earlier books, The Curious World of Seaweed and An Ocean Garden: The Secret Life of Seaweed. Her work brings together art, design, science and environmental history.

Iselin is co-director of Above/Below, a campaign that raises awareness of underwater kelp forests. She serves as the primary writer and content creator for its educational web-based books, including The Mysterious World of Bull Kelp and The Alluring World of Olympia Oysters. She has also created exhibitions and installations that bring seaweed imagery and marine science into gallery spaces.

events.title: Women Behind the Camera During the Silent Era with Dwight M. Cleveland
events.address: 155 S. River Street Santa Cruz, CA 95060
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerDwight Cleveland CollectionWomen Behind the Camera During the Silent Era with Dwight M. Cleveland
Thursday, November 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM The 418 Project, Santa Cruz, California

Join film historian, author, and renowned movie poster collector Dwight M. Cleveland for an illustrated lecture exploring the overlooked contributions of women who helped establish the American film industry during the silent era.
Drawing from nearly 50 years of collecting, Cleveland will present rare historical film posters and lobby cards, with particular attention to the women who worked as directors, screenwriters, and producers during cinema’s formative decades. His collection includes more than 10,000 silent film lobby cards documenting the careers of over 1,000 women, many of whom have received little recognition in traditional film histories.
Cleveland’s collections have been exhibited at Poster House in New York City and the Norton Museum of Art. His archival materials have also contributed to Dartmouth College’s Early Cinema Compendium, a research initiative supported by the National Endowment for the Humanities.
The presentation will examine the historical significance of these surviving materials and their role in documenting women’s foundational contributions to cinema.
A limited number of copies of Cleveland’s book, CINEMA ON PAPER: The Graphic Genius of Movie Posters (Assouline, 2019), will be available for purchase and signing.

events.title: A Chorus Line: Teen Edition
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerKeith Carames

A Chorus Line: Teen Edition is a stunning concept musical capturing the spirit and tension of a Broadway ensemble audition, adapted for students.

A Chorus Line is a stunning concept musical capturing the spirit and tension of a Broadway ensemble audition. Exploring the inner lives and poignant ambitions of professional Broadway performers, the show features one powerhouse number after another, including “What I Did for Love,” “One,” “I Can Do That,” “At the Ballet,” “The Music and the Mirror” and “I Hope I Get It.” A brilliantly complex fusion of song, dance and compellingly authentic drama, the show was instantly recognized as a classic. A Chorus Line: Teen Edition is a full-length version of the Pulitzer Prize-winning musical, adapted for performance by students with family audiences. Every aspect of the show has been developed specifically for student performers: dialogue and content are age-appropriate, dance sequences are of a length befitting student dancers. Directed by Keith Carames with Music Direction by Jorell Chavez and Choreography by Vince Chan.

events.title: Angels in America, Part One: Millennium Approaches
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPhoto by Crystal LiuIn the first part of Tony Kushner’s Pulitzer-winning epic, set in 1980’s New York City, a gay man is abandoned by his lover when he contracts the AIDS virus, and a closeted Mormon lawyer’s marriage to his pill-popping wife stalls. Other characters include the infamous McCarthy-ite lawyer Roy Cohn, Ethel Rosenberg, a former drag queen who works as a nurse, and an angel.
Between its 1993 Broadway premiere and its 2017 National Theatre revival, Angels’ mythical status has expanded, onstage and off. But to director and actor John Fisher, this play is best experienced when presented up close, with its human heartbreaks and joys mere feet from the audience. “[Theatre Rhinoceros] is ‘IMAX’ theatre – it’s immediate, it’s right there, you could touch the actors. It’s always been staged as an epic, as opposed to a lived experience. And I don’t believe it was written as an epic, it was written as a ‘fantasia’ – and fantasy is immersive, not witnessed.”

events.title: $25 Encore Screening: “El Sett” + Umm Kulthum’s Story
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerImage courtesy of Watermelon PicturesThe 30th Arab Film Festival opens on Thursday November 5th with El Sett, Marwan Hamed’s sweeping cinematic portrait of legendary Egyptian singer Umm Kulthum, one of the most celebrated and influential artists in the history of the Arab world.
The 6 pm Opening Night screening is almost sold out, so we opened an Encore Screening for all night owls who want to watch El Sett!

PLEASE NOTE: The Encore Screening is offered at a reduced price because it includes only the movie (there won’t be a program before or a performance after)
You are invited to join us in your best attire, just like you would have dressed to see Umm Kulthum perform at her legendary 1967 performance at Paris’s Olympia! Let’s transform the evening into a memorable tribute to the most iconic Arab singer of all times.
About EL SETT
Starring Mona Zaki as Umm Kulthum, the film traces her extraordinary journey from a childhood singing in rural Egypt, where she performed disguised as a boy, to her rise as the Arab world’s most iconic voice. The story culminates around her historic 1967 performance at Paris’s Olympia, while exploring the ambition, sacrifice, resilience, and defiance of social conventions that shaped her remarkable life.

events.title: Haiku in the Garden – Autumn
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerMarin Art and Garden CenterJoin us to savor the poetry of the season, in this free gathering hosted by Jayne McPherson.
Gardens have an essential and ubiquitous place in lyric poetry. The great poet Kahlil Gibran called friendship a garden, one where planted seeds are sown “with love and reap thanksgiving.”

During this season, let’s follow his poetic lead and look up at distant mountains that frame the lazy lady on the horizon. Let’s remind ourselves of the middle pond’s pink and white lotus blossoms-that they float night and day under the sun or moonlight. Let’s notice how the water fountain’s splash undulates in ringlets; how, inside the iron gate, blossoms protrude as promises kept in heirloom roses; how a giving-tree oak allows another woodpecker or squirrel to sneak substance and nest.
Haiku offers beauty in form and empathy. And like a harvest, it can evoke awe or perhaps simply ahhh. When we seek pause in the natural world, we may remember our breath and breathe more deeply. We may tune in, feel our heartbeat, sense a door opening as we pause before a sunning lizard or grazing deer.
Writing haiku is a quiet way to savor these Garden gifts.
This is our third anniversary writing circle and will feature haikuist, David Watts. His poetry has been published widely. It includes two books, Dream Tree & Seed Kites.
David Watts is recognized by Haiku Poets of Northern California.

Featured photo by Sachi CunninghamHeavy Water Collective Presents: Ocean Beach brings together 24 photographers who turn their lenses toward the Pacific, finding pockets of magic amidst a vast liquid field of chaos.

Some of these works play with the juxtaposition of ocean wilderness and concrete cityscapes, framing surfers speeding down powerful waves with electrical wiring and concrete in the foreground. events.title: ZooLights at San Francisco Zoo (Nov. 6-Jan 3)
events.description:
San Francisco Zoo & GardensSan Francisco Zoo & Gardens is thrilled to announce its all-new, two-month-long ZooLights evening holiday program that will light up the Zoo in spectacular fashion from November 6 through January 3, 2027. The nighttime event represents the return of ZooLights, which the Zoo last hosted in 2018.

“The Zoo is the perfect venue for a safe, outdoor holiday lights experience,” said Cassandra Costello, CEO and Executive Director. “We have taken this event to the next level, creating 14 dazzling zones, with winter, botanical or animal-themed components. It’s going to be truly breathtaking, and a great experience for the entire family.”

In addition to traditional holiday zones, where guests will walk through awe-inspiring lighted tunnels and stroll among giant candy canes, giant ornaments and gift boxes, there’s an entire frozen zone, with 10-foot-tall icicles, sparkling snowflakes, a frozen forest, a massive ice throne and frozen sleigh for that perfect family photo.

“The effect will be magical,” said Costello. “Overall, ZooLights will have more than one million lights, and the walk-through areas include amazing photo ops, and nods to the City of San Francisco with a Golden Gate Bridge and the iconic cable car.”

Whimsical animal shapes and scenes will dot the landscape, using 2D and 3D illuminations of a rhino and gorilla, even a tree full of ring-tailed lemurs. Vibrantly colored, larger-than-life butterflies are part of an enchanting botanical pathway,...

In this rollicking autobiographical comedy, Janet moves from Colorado to San Francisco in 1972, where a closed-head injury, late-in-life love, even-later-in-life parenthood, and a divorce await her, along with a right-wing coup led by one of the seven subpersonalities in her psyche. Rosie wants new clothes and skin care; Mauve wants writers’ conferences. Add the shock of becoming an elder, and something has got to give.

events.title: In/Decision – A Contemporary Circus Show
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerGreat Star TheaterCheapFun Promo Code: DecideSF for $5 discount
From the producers of Memoir comes a unique new theatrical circus experience.

In/Decision is an exploration of the moments that define us, the leaps we take, the risks we avoid, the paths we choose without knowing where they lead. Through a seamless weaving of breathtaking aerials, acrobatics and storytelling, this original production invites audiences into the fragile space between choice and consequence.
Each act balances on the edge of possibility: releasing the bar, shifting weight, moving forward, or taking a step back. A character speaks, or stays silent. In these suspended moments, worlds are made and unmade.
Poetic, visceral, and deeply human, In/Decision asks: Are we guided by destiny, or do we build it step by step?
Come join us, and decide.
Doors open one hour before the show starts.
No intermission.

San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

events.title: Free Filipino “Manilatown” Film Double Feature + Q&As at SFMOMA
events.venue: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA)
events.description:
Manilatown Heritage Foundation“Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy.” brings two generations of San Francisco’s Manilatown and International Hotel history to the big screen at SFMOMA for a special FREE double-feature presentation.
At 1 PM, experience the San Francisco premiere of the newly enhanced and restored edition of Curtis Choy’s landmark 1983 documentary, “The Fall of the I-Hotel”. The film chronicles the decade-long struggle to save San Francisco’s International Hotel and the August 4, 1977 eviction of its predominantly Filipino and Chinese elder tenants. Following the screening, filmmaker Curtis Choy joins co-producers of the enhanced edition for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.
At 3 PM, experience the premiere of “Manilatown Manang”, the story of Jeanette Gandionco Lazam-artist, activist, and one of the few women who lived in the International Hotel as a Tenant Defender during the historic anti-eviction movement. The film follows Jeanette’s journey from the I-Hotel struggle through a lifetime of activism, art, and community. Following the premiere, Jeanette Lazam joins the film’s producers and creative team for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

Together, the films create a powerful dialogue between past and present: audiences first encounter Jeanette as a young activist in Choy’s historic documentary, then experience the continuation of her story in Manilatown Manang.

events.title: Free “Wood Street” Film Screening on Oakland’s Unhoused + Q&A (SF Main Library)
events.description:
Caron CreightonWOOD STREET follows a year in the life of Oakland’s largest unhoused encampment as its residents face an imminent eviction that threatens to dismantle their community. As notices appear and police move in, residents organize — building barricades, filing lawsuits, and protesting at City Hall to fight for their right to stay. Told through immersive verité, the film places viewers inside the encampment, capturing the urgency, resilience, and emotional toll of collective resistance. At its center are John and LaMonté, whose bond is tested as pressure mounts — LaMonté’s mental health deteriorates while John struggles to remain sober. When the eviction comes, the community is physically erased, but its spirit endures.
The film will be followed by a Q&A with the film team, members of the Wood Street community and the editor of Street Sheet newspaper.

events.title: Free Night Walking Tour of Chinatown Alleyways + North Beach
events.address: Bush Street &, Grant Ave, San Francisco, CA 94108
events.description:
Filip ToddAfter dark, Chinatown quiets down. That’s when this walk starts.
It’s a free 90-minute evening tour that begins at the Dragon Gate and works up through Chinatown’s back alleys to the point where the neighbourhood turns into North Beach. Along the way: the old tong buildings on Waverly Place, the gambling alleyways, a Bruce Lee mural, Jack Kerouac Alley and City Lights Bookstore. It ends at Golden Boy Pizza.
Two neighbourhoods pressed up against each other for more than a century, and the seam between them is the most interesting part of either.

The tour is free in the real sense — no ticket, nothing paid up front. At the end you decide what it was worth, and there’s no obligation.
Guided in English. Meets at the Dragon Gate, corner of Bush Street and Grant Avenue.

Join Dardick at San Francisco’s Adobe Books for a free reading and discussion of his new memoir, The Adventures of Superfreak: My Childhood on the Hippie Trail (Running Wild Press, 2026).

The book is a child’s-eye view of the counterculture, filled with adventure, humor, wonder, and instability. As San Francisco approaches the 60th anniversary of the Summer of Love in 2027, Dardick offers an unusual perspective on that era: the children who were along for the ride.
A former San Francisco resident who spent nearly three decades in Berkeley, Dardick wrote much of the memoir in the Bay Area.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFred BrillYou don’t want to miss the November 10 Conundrum Chronicles StorySlam! (The Marsh Theater– 1062 Valencia Street, SF)
Put your name in the hat for a chance to tell a true five-minute story; be the judge; or kick back and enjoy magic of live storytelling!

THEME: TURNING POINT Some turning points arrive like a car crash—sudden, loud, impossible to miss. Others are quiet: a sentence someone said, a choice you almost didn’t make, a morning that looked like any other morning until it wasn’t. We want to hear about the moment your story bent in a new direction. What did you leave behind? What did you walk toward? Looking back now, did you know that everything was about to change?

A returning storyteller at the Nutshell and Redwood Nights, she has been seen at Oakland Story Slam, Pretty Good Stories, Queens Story, Lit Quake, The Moth, the Marsh – Tell it on Tuesdays and Monday Nights at the Marsh.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: Handel’s The Power of Music (Stanford)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerDennis BoltCan Music Change the Course of History?
Three centuries ago, George Frideric Handel explored a bold idea: that music can change how people think, feel, and act.

Music Director Peter Whelan and Philharmonia Baroque Orchestra & Chorale open the 2026/27 season with Handel’s The Power of Music, featuring Alexander’s Feast, a vocal and choral masterpiece inspired by a legendary banquet marking Alexander the Great’s victory over Persia. As the feast unfolds, poet-musician Timotheus uses music to influence the conqueror and change the course of history.
Bay Area audiences will be first in the U.S. to hear Handel’s 1742 Dublin version, performed on period instruments and in the style of the time.

The San Francisco Transgender Film Festival (SFTFF) celebrates 29 years of innovative, experimental, and outside-the-box films by transgender and gender-nonconforming filmmakers.

Spanning 12-days from November 12-22 and comprised of seven short film programs showcasing 37 films, SFTFF 2026 will be a hybrid festival, presented both in person and online, and featuring a range of genres from documentaries and politics to animation, dance, music, romance, coming-of-age tales, and thrillers.
SFTFF will host in-person programs Nov. 12-14 at the Roxie Theater, 3117 16th St., SF and will offer on demand access to each of the programs through Nov. 22nd. Films are closed captioned for Deaf and hard-of-hearing audiences; tickets are $0-$50, sliding scale/donation-based, inclusive of fees.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerDennis BoltCan Music Change the Course of History?
Three centuries ago, George Frideric Handel explored a bold idea: that music can change how people think, feel, and act.

Music Director Peter Whelan and Philharmonia Baroque Orchestra & Chorale open the 2026/27 season with Handel’s The Power of Music, featuring Alexander’s Feast, a vocal and choral masterpiece inspired by a legendary banquet marking Alexander the Great’s victory over Persia. As the feast unfolds, poet-musician Timotheus uses music to influence the conqueror and change the course of history.
Bay Area audiences will be first in the U.S. to hear Handel’s 1742 Dublin version, performed on period instruments and in the style of the time.

events.address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Prokofiev’s “Romeo & Juliet” w/ the SF Symphony (Nov. 13–15)
SF Symphony
Prokofiev’s ballet music for Romeo and Juliet is every bit as singular as the Shakespeare tragedy that inspired it: Savage and sensual, tragic and comic, it conveys all the passion of the play and loses none of its ambiguity. Debuting French conductor Marie Jacquot leads the Orchestra in the first SF Symphony performances of Andromède, by her underrated fellow countrywoman Augusta Holmès.
The symphonic poem infuses ancient Greek myth with Wagnerian grandeur. Inspired by the music of early Christianity, Ottorino Respighi pulls off medieval plainsong with 20th-century pizzazz in his spellbinding Concerto gregoriano. Japanese violinist Sayaka Shoji summons up all of its enormous expressive power.
Prokofiev’s Romeo and Juliet

events.title: Echoes of the Seasons: A Piano Dialogue Between East and West
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLExplore how Eastern and Western composers interpret the seasons across different musical traditions. Western selections express vivid natural imagery, from Vivaldi’s dynamic storms to Tchaikovsky’s romantic winter scenes and the reflective mood of Autumn Leaves. These works translate the physical world into sound through color, emotion and narrative.
Eastern musical philosophy centers Yijing (意境), an aesthetic that blends atmosphere, poetry and spiritual resonance. Rooted in the Chinese pentatonic scale, this approach moves beyond direct depiction, inviting listeners to experience nature as a contemplative reflection of the self.

Through classical masterworks, jazz and traditional Chinese repertoire, this lecture‑recital highlights how artistic languages encounter one another across cultures. The program invites audiences to hear how different musical philosophies interpret the seasons and how these perspectives generate deeper understanding of memory, place and expression.

events.title: Fort Point Beer Co Presents: Manzanita Night
events.description:
Fort Point Beer Co

A one-night celebration at Fort Point Valencia to honor our favorite fall tradition: the release of our Manzanita Smoked Altbier.

Join us as we kick off Manzanita season with a night we hope becomes an annual tradition. The cask taps at 5:30pm. Be there for the toast and first pour.
Brewed with charred local manzanita branches, Manzanita is a beautiful dark beer that’s light-bodied and somehow nutty, herbal, sweet and savory all at once. Decisively autumnal without relying on the clichés of the season, it’s our very Northern California take on the classic smoked beers of Northern Bavaria and a Fort Point cult favorite.

Cask-conditioned Manzanita: Gravity-poured from a cask on the bar, the way they still serve it in Bamberg, the world’s smoked beer capital. Get it before the cask runs dry.
Smoked beer flights: Manzanita (cask & draft) alongside selections from Bamberg’s historic Schlenkerla and Freigeist, the experimental brewery that we collabed with on the very first Manzanita batch.
Manzanita steins: Rastal ceramic half liters, custom printed with the Manzanita icon. Fill one at the bar and take it home. Limited run, while supplies last.
First 4-packs of the season: Sold to go before they’re available anywhere else.

events.title: Free 2026 Art Week Opening: Kinetic Sculpture Show “Abiogenesis” at SF’s Heron Arts
events.description:
Image courtesy of artists.Heron Arts is pleased to announce Abiogenesis, a duo exhibition featuring Philip Beesley and Casey Curran. The opening reception for Abiogenesis is Saturday, November 14th, 2026 from 6-9pm. It is free and open to the public and will be part of San Francisco Art Week. The exhibition will be on view to the public until January 24th, by appointment only.

Abiogenesis brings together the work of Philip Beesley and Casey Curran around an elusive phenomenon: the emergence of life from inert matter. Their work assembles unmistakably artificial elements that, in their cellular forms and gentle movement, begin to suggest life. Lacework becomes membrane. Scaffolds of repeating cells become skeletons of organisms. Glowing, shimmering light evokes the pulses of nature. Mechanical gestures appear to breathe, bloom, and reach into the world.

Intimations of life within Beesley’s and Curran’s sculptures suggest that living form can emerge from the matter of the earth. Beesley and Curran probe this threshold through myth, science, and sensitive sculptural expression.

Artist Bios

Philip Beesley is a Canadian artist whose sculptures explore the threshold between inert matter and living form. At the heart of his work are glowing, pulsing, precious structures composed of innumerable finely crafted elements. events.description:
Prokofiev’s “Romeo & Juliet” w/ the SF Symphony (Nov. 13–15)
SF Symphony
Prokofiev’s ballet music for Romeo and Juliet is every bit as singular as the Shakespeare tragedy that inspired it: Savage and sensual, tragic and comic, it conveys all the passion of the play and loses none of its ambiguity. Debuting French conductor Marie Jacquot leads the Orchestra in the first SF Symphony performances of Andromède, by her underrated fellow countrywoman Augusta Holmès.
The symphonic poem infuses ancient Greek myth with Wagnerian grandeur. Inspired by the music of early Christianity, Ottorino Respighi pulls off medieval plainsong with 20th-century pizzazz in his spellbinding Concerto gregoriano. Japanese violinist Sayaka Shoji summons up all of its enormous expressive power.

Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.
